correspondence.component_scope: Unnamed selected headward approach and its connection to the receiving Kongakut River
correspondence.finding: The chosen opening is a small mapped feeder entering an unnamed valley channel. Its southward bend, northeastern approach, intervening eastern bends and downstream confluence are visible in the original opening and upper-west maps. The river arriving from the southwest is labelled Kongakut River; the selected approach is not independently given that name. The component range is an orientation grouping, not a formal hydronym-boundary assignment.
correspondence.correspondence: Unnamed selected headward approach and its connection to the receiving Kongakut River

correspondence.component_scope: Receiving river and braided eastward upper valley
correspondence.finding: Repeated directly placed river labels and the connected channel network support the eastward upper Kongakut corridor through the remaining western and eastward bends. No lake, reservoir, glacier or managed transfer interrupts the selected route in the inspected cartography.
correspondence.correspondence: Receiving river and braided eastward upper valley

correspondence.component_scope: Northeast and northward upper trunk with tributary junctions
correspondence.finding: The braided Kongakut turns northeast and north through the mountain valley. Drain Creek is an independently labelled incoming tributary; its mapped junction and the other intervening joins are visible. The selected route continues along the named trunk rather than up Drain Creek or across a divide.
correspondence.correspondence: Northeast and northward upper trunk with tributary junctions

correspondence.component_scope: Middle northward trunk, eastern tributary confluences and northwest bend
correspondence.finding: The connected braided main valley is visible past the eastern tributary joins and around its substantial northwest bend. Baseline Creek joins from the southwest on this northwest-trending reach. Named or unnamed tributaries outside the selected line are not assigned the representative river name.
correspondence.correspondence: Middle northward trunk, eastern tributary confluences and northwest bend

correspondence.component_scope: Northern mountain-front exit, coastal plain and selected eastern distributary approach
correspondence.finding: The original lower map connects the northwest bend to the northward coastal braided river. It shows the distributary split and the selected northeastern/eastern Kongakut branch toward Siku Lagoon. The western lagoon outlet and adjacent independent river corridors are not substituted for the selected route.
correspondence.correspondence: Northern mountain-front exit, coastal plain and selected eastern distributary approach

correspondence.component_scope: Selected Kongakut delta branch and Siku Lagoon receiving setting
correspondence.finding: The final selected internal part remains within the labelled Kongakut delta network. The original detailed delta map shows distributary channels continuing into directly labelled Siku Lagoon. The endpoint is not asserted to be the exact present-day mouth. The terminal conclusion follows the mapped network beyond the generalized endpoint at ordinary delta scale.
correspondence.correspondence: Selected Kongakut delta branch and Siku Lagoon receiving setting

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen northeastern opening and upper Taylor Creek hook
correspondence.finding: The short initial approach corresponds to an unnamed north-running tributary valley entering upper Taylor Creek from the south. The original opening detail shows that tributary connection and the subsequent northern turn into the westward Taylor Creek corridor. Taylor Creek is directly labeled on the receiving channel. The selected start is not asserted to be the natural source of Taylor Creek, and the unnamed feeder receives no invented hydronym.

correspondence.component_scope: Taylor Creek westward continuation and Kougarok joining setting
correspondence.finding: The mapped Taylor Creek continues west and southwest past the Midnight Creek and other tributary joining setting toward the Taylor settlement/airport area and the Washington Creek approach. The channel continuing south is directly labeled Kougarok River. North Star Ditch is separately mapped in this setting; its nearby label is not substituted for the natural river corridor or assigned to the whole selection.

correspondence.component_scope: Kougarok middle valley and tributary junctions
correspondence.finding: The selected south-running interval corresponds to the repeatedly labeled Kougarok River valley. The original map distinguishes the eastern North Fork Kougarok River junction, the western Left Fork Kougarok River approach and the Windy Creek junction farther south. The river continues through the valley toward the lowland; the separate Garfield Creek drainage to the east is not substituted for it.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Kougarok and joining Kuzitrin River
correspondence.finding: The lower selected Kougarok reach passes through the meandering lowland and joins the directly labeled Kuzitrin River arriving from the east/northeast. Downstream correspondence follows the western Kuzitrin course past the road/Hooligan setting. The source shows the actual joining channels, rather than only a basin label or nearby place-name.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Kuzitrin bends, Pilgrim joining setting and broad mouth
correspondence.finding: Readable original mapping shows the selected Kuzitrin corridor west through the bends by Igloo, the lower junction network with Pilgrim River from the southeast, and the widening northwestern continuation into the broad Kuzitrin mouth. Davidsons Slough, Lake Omiaktalik and Kaviruk River are separately labeled neighboring or connecting features. Their names are not applied to the entire modeled line, and lake proximity is not used as proof of a selected Lake Omiaktalik passage.

correspondence.component_scope: Kuzitrin entry and Imuruk Basin waterbody passage
correspondence.finding: The broad Kuzitrin mouth connects to the eastern Imuruk Basin waterbody, and the chosen westward passage lies within that connected basin at ordinary scale. The Agiapuk River enters the basin independently from the north. The Imuruk Basin identity remains distinct from the Kuzitrin river component; the composite map also places Tuksuk Channel labels over parts of the connected waterbody, which are not treated as precise naming boundaries.

correspondence.component_scope: Western basin outlet, Tuksuk Channel and actual terminal
correspondence.finding: The selected western turn corresponds to the mapped outlet from Imuruk Basin through the constricted Tuksuk Channel, continuing north into the eastern end of Grantley Harbor at the actual selected terminal. The map shows a continuous open-water passage through this constriction. The harbor and channel are retained as separate named coastal-water components; no contemporary tidal direction, exact shoreline or surveyed mouth vertex is inferred.

correspondence.component_scope: Southwestern selected opening and northeast feeder
correspondence.finding: No acquired detailed primary map covers this selected opening. No natural source, lake identity or hydraulic connector is inferred from the modeled line.

correspondence.component_scope: Long eastward headward course and its eastern elbow
correspondence.finding: The field report identifies Kinushseo Lake as a distinct sampled lake in the region, but its generalized Figure 1 does not establish the selected entry, exit, route through any waterbody or complete eastward feeder connection. No lake is adopted as a selected component on proximity alone.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern north-turning approach into the detailed-map boundary
correspondence.finding: Only the northern portion of encoded part 13 is within the acquired map. The southern approach and its connection across the uncovered interval remain material-pending; the mapped river’s identity is not extended across that gap.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle Kinushseo trunk and side-stream joins
correspondence.finding: Direct labels, the continuous north-running channel, west/east bends, northeastward central leg and eastward elbow, side-stream joins and the adjoining-map transition correspond to the selection. Separate tributaries and surrounding wetland ponds are not renamed. No selected reservoir, glacier or managed connector is established in this inspected interval.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower river and selected estuarine transition
correspondence.finding: The selected narrow north-running lower river follows the channel into its widening and northwest turn. The terminal lies at the eastern head of the wider estuarine reach rather than at the offshore end of the full estuary. Exact current banks, tidal limits, branch allocation and a surveyed mouth vertex are not assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Receiving-water context beyond the selection
correspondence.finding: The mapped Kinushseo estuarine continuation leads northwest toward the coastal bay beside Little Cape and Hudson Bay. Sutton River is a separately labelled western entry. This downstream continuation is not silently appended to the selected feature.

correspondence.component_scope: Extreme western El Mirador–La Rueda plain opening and northeastward approach to the mapped upper drainage
correspondence.finding: The historical original depicts this land corridor but does not delineate a continuous watercourse along the entire selected western opening. The independent thesis distinguishes natural streams, canals and depressions; its regional canal map and separate depression-connection example do not positively establish this complete selected through-link.
correspondence.hydraulic_limit: Neither a continuous natural river nor a particular engineered drainage canal is established for the opening.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern upper river arm past La Fortuna toward the Brandsen-area confluence
correspondence.finding: The original topographic image shows the northern channel approach and its connection south of Brandsen. The thesis hydrology section distinguishes the northern Samborombón Chico/San Vicente arm from the southern Samborombón arm, and its original figure 3-27 identifies the Chico channel near Brandsen. This bounds the upper-component candidate without fixing the name transition or repairing the missing western opening.
correspondence.name_scope: Do not extend Samborombón Chico or San Vicente over the unresolved western opening, or assign an exact name-change vertex.

correspondence.component_scope: Brandsen–Jeppener–Altamirano middle receiving corridor and tributary junctions
correspondence.finding: Readable original cartography follows the receiving channel southeast past Jeppener and Altamirano, including the Abascay-side junction and the major road crossing. Tributaries remain distinct from the selected through-river. The neighboring El Sauce and Chascomús lake areas are not used as selected lake passages.

correspondence.component_scope: Don Cipriano–Las Varillas middle/lower meandering and floodplain corridor
correspondence.finding: The continuous original river trace, direct Samborombón label, bends and tributary junctions support this selected corridor. Thesis figures 2-21 and 2-22 independently show named main-channel bends and a floodplain-waterbody passage. Generalized mapping does not establish present water levels, every small distributary choice, or permanent lake-through flow.

correspondence.component_scope: Pipinas-side coastal plain, lower southward bend and estuarine mouth
correspondence.finding: Historical cartography follows the lower meandering river into the coastal margin. Thesis figures 2-23 and 2-24 show the named lower channel and its own mouth into Bahía Samborombón, north of and separate from the Río Salado mouth. The selected terminal is consistent with that Samborombón outlet at corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Lakes, wetlands, managed drainage and reservoir context
correspondence.finding: Floodplain depressions, temporary inundation, channels and rectifications are documented. The studied examples are not permission to infer the unresolved opening as a canal connection. No selected reservoir passage is established. Nearby named lakes are not automatically part of the selected route.
